371: ## 13. Acceptance Criteria

372: 

373: Dates and clocks in tests are injected, so results are deterministic.

374: 

375: ### Accounts and security

376: - [ ] **AC-01** (SEC1) Registering stores an Argon2id hash (the stored value starts with `$argon2id$`), never returns or logs the password, and returns 409 `email_taken` for a duplicate email, compared case-insensitively (`A@x.com` and `a@x.com` conflict).

377: - [ ] **AC-02** (SEC1) A password of 11 characters is rejected with 422; 12 and 128 characters are accepted; 129 is rejected.

378: - [ ] **AC-03** (SEC2, SEC5) Login sets an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie (and `Secure` over TLS); a wrong email and a wrong password return the same status and body (`invalid_credentials`).

379: - [ ] **AC-04** (SEC6) The 6th failed login within 15 minutes for one account returns 429 with `Retry-After`; after the window passes (injected clock) a correct login succeeds.

380: - [ ] **AC-05** (SEC2) After logout, the old session cookie returns 401 on every endpoint.

381: - [ ] **AC-06** (SEC3) A POST, PATCH or DELETE without a valid CSRF token returns 403 `csrf_failed`; GET requests are unaffected.

382: - [ ] **AC-07** (SEC7) A login over plain HTTP from a non-localhost client returns 403 `tls_required`; over TLS, or from localhost, it works; a forged forwarded-protocol header from an untrusted client is ignored.

383: - [ ] **AC-08** (SEC4) *Ownership matrix.* For every user-owned endpoint (derived automatically from the route table), user B requesting, changing or deleting user A's resource by ID gets a 404 identical to a missing ID, list endpoints never include A's items, and A's data is unchanged in the database.

384: - [ ] **AC-09** (SEC8) A request body containing `user_id` (or any unknown field) is rejected with 422.

385: - [ ] **AC-10** (SEC8) The string `'; DROP TABLE users;--` saved in a note is stored and returned literally, and all tables remain intact.

386: - [ ] **AC-11** (SEC9) Responses carry the Content-Security-Policy, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy` and frame-protection headers; CORS allows only the configured origin.

387: - [ ] **AC-12** (SEC10) A script finds no secret patterns in tracked files and no tracked `.env`; in production mode the application refuses to start with a missing secret or one equal to the `.env.example` placeholder.

388: - [ ] **AC-13** (SEC8) A request body above 1 MB returns 413.

389: - [ ] **AC-14** (SEC11) `pip-audit` and `npm audit` show no known high or critical vulnerabilities at release; the results are recorded.

390:

531: | FR-11 Grocery list | AC-77 to AC-81 |

532: | FR-12 Nutrition logging | AC-82 to AC-84 |

533: | FR-13 Combined dashboard | AC-85 |

534: | FR-14 Insights | AC-86, AC-87 |

535: | FR-15 Data controls | AC-34, AC-88, AC-89 |

536: 

537: ## 15. Non-Functional Requirements

538: 

539: | Area | Requirement |

540: | --- | --- |

541: | Correctness | Exact decimals for all calculations; one place for each formula; formulas live in `app/domain` |

542: | Reliability | Multi-row writes (workouts, plans, logs) run in transactions |

543: | Performance | Paginated history, the indexes in section 6, and the targets in AC-70 and AC-103 |

544: | Maintainability | Thin routers, services for rules, repositories for queries, enforced by AC-98 |

545: | Explainability | Every plan exposes its targets, constraints, scoring weights and data provenance |

546: | Accessibility | Section 9 and AC-90 to AC-94 |

547: | Privacy | Collect only what is needed; export and delete (S10, FR-15) |

548: | Testability | Injected clock, seeded fixtures, deterministic planner |

549: 

550: ## 16. Testing Strategy

551: 

552: | Layer | What it checks | Tooling |

553: | --- | --- | --- |

554: | Unit (domain) | Units, e1RM, volume, PRs, nutrient maths, targets, filters, scoring, aggregation, with the worked numbers above | pytest |

555: | Property | Allergen exclusion, totals equal sums, deterministic plans, ownership matrix | pytest with Hypothesis |

556: | Database | Constraints, cascades, restrictions, transactions, migrations, index use | pytest against a real PostgreSQL (a Compose service), never SQLite |

557: | API | Authentication, CSRF, validation, ownership, errors, pagination | pytest with HTTPX or TestClient |

558: | Frontend | Forms, validation messages, states, substitution flow, chart alternatives | Vitest and Testing Library |

559: | End to end | The full journey, keyboard-only logging, 360-pixel layout, accessibility scan, hidden-calories mode | Playwright and axe |

560: | Safety | Section 3 rules, banned-word scan, minors and floor behaviour | pytest and the end-to-end suite |

561: | Quality gates | Lint, type checks, coverage, OpenAPI type freshness, secret scan, dependency audit | CI |

562: | Deployment | Container build, health, restart, persistence, backup and restore, TLS | Docker, a smoke script, a manual second-device check |

563: 

564: Expected values come from the calculations written in the acceptance criteria, not from copying the application's output.

565: 

566: ## 17. Build Order

567: 

568: Build in this order, because each step depends on the one before it. A step is done when its acceptance criteria pass. There are no time estimates; go as fast as the tests allow.

569: 

570: | Step | Build | Acceptance criteria |

571: | --- | --- | --- |

572: | 1 | Repo and tooling setup, CI skeleton, ER diagram, and a walking-skeleton Compose stack (database, a backend with `/api/health`, a placeholder frontend) | AC-97 (start), AC-105 (skeleton) |

573: | 2 | The pure domain functions: units, e1RM, volume, PRs, nutrient maths, targets, aggregation, scoring, with their unit tests | AC-16, AC-39 to AC-41, AC-43, AC-45 to AC-47, AC-63, AC-64, AC-77 to AC-79, AC-19 to AC-21 (maths) |

574: | 3 | Database models and migrations, authentication, sessions, CSRF, rate limiting, TLS rule, and the ownership-test harness | AC-01 to AC-13, AC-15, AC-97, AC-98, AC-104 |

575: | 4 | Catalogue and seed: exercises, foods, recipes, provenance, allergens, validators | AC-48 to AC-55 |

576: | 5 | Workouts and routines: API and UI, history, pagination, edit and delete, the logger | AC-29 to AC-38, AC-90 to AC-96 (for these screens) |

577: | 6 | Strength analytics and charts | AC-40 to AC-42, AC-44, AC-93 |

578: | 7 | Nutrition profile, targets and the safety rules, with the settings UI | AC-17 to AC-28 |

579: | 8 | The plan generator, with `infeasible` explanations and the plan UI | AC-56 to AC-72 |

580: | 9 | Substitutions, manual edits, and the grocery list | AC-73 to AC-81 |

1: ---
2: name: managing-python-dependencies
3: description: |
4:   Ensures proper Python dependency management, avoiding global `pip install` and
5:   adhering to project-specific tooling.
6: 
7:   Use this skill if any of the following are true:
8:     1. Attempting to run `pip install {package_name}`.
9:     2. Python packages or dependencies need to be added or modified.
10:     3. Initiating a new Python project.
11:     4. Creating a new notebook, even if just using BigQuery cells.
12:     5. Generating Python code that includes `import` statements for third-party libraries.
13:     6. Before executing Python scripts via the terminal to ensure the correct virtual environment is active.
14: license: Apache-2.0
15: metadata:
16:   version: v1
17:   publisher: google
18: ---
19: 
20: # Python Dependency Management Rule
21: 
22: > [!CAUTION]
23: >
24: > **BEFORE any `pip install`**: You MUST first detect the project's existing
25: > dependency manager and use it correctly. Do NOT override the project's
26: > established tooling.
27: 
28: ## Dependency Manager Detection
29: 
30: Before installing ANY Python package, check the workspace for these files **in
31: priority order**:
32: 
33: 1.  **Signal:** `uv.lock` or `pyproject.toml` with `[tool.uv]`
34:     *   **Tool:** **uv**
35:     *   **Install:** `uv add <package>`
36:     *   **Setup:** `uv sync`
37: 2.  **Signal:** `pyproject.toml` with `[tool.poetry]`
38:     *   **Tool:** **Poetry**
39:     *   **Install:** `poetry add <package>`
40:     *   **Setup:** `poetry install`
41: 3.  **Signal:** `Pipfile`
42:     *   **Tool:** **Pipenv**
43:     *   **Install:** `pipenv install <package>`
44:     *   **Setup:** `pipenv install`
45: 4.  **Signal:** `environment.yml`
46:     *   **Tool:** **Conda**
47:     *   **Install:** `conda install <package>`
48:     *   **Setup:** `conda env create -f environment.yml`
49: 5.  **Signal:** `requirements.txt` only
50:     *   **Tool:** **venv + pip**
51:     *   **Install:** `.venv/bin/pip install <package>`
52:     *   **Setup:** `.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt`
53: 6.  **Signal:** None of the above
54:     *   **Tool:** **venv + pip** (default)
55:     *   **Install:** `.venv/bin/pip install <package>`
56:     *   **Setup:** `.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt`
57: 
58: ## Default: venv + pip
59: 
60: If no dependency manager is detected, use **venv + pip + requirements.txt** as
61: the default:
62: 
63: ```bash
64: # Initialize environment
65: python3 -m venv .venv
66: 
67: # Add dependencies
68: .venv/bin/pip install <package>
69: 
70: # Preserve state
71: .venv/bin/pip freeze > requirements.txt
72: ```
73: 
74: **Rules for venv + pip workflow:**
75: 
76: -   Always use `.venv/bin/pip` or `.venv/bin/python` (explicit path).
77: -   After installing, run: `.venv/bin/pip freeze > requirements.txt`.
78: -   When setting up: `.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt`.
79: 
80: ## Prohibited
81: 
82: -   **NEVER** run `pip install` globally
83: -   **NEVER** override an existing dependency manager with a different one
84:

### [LEARN] Module 1: e1RM, Volume, and PR Detection (Spec §5.2, AC-39–41, AC-43)

Tests have been written in [test_domain_strength.py](file:///c:/Users/abhir/OneDrive/Desktop/AIDS/Gym%20workout%20logger/backend/tests/test_domain_strength.py) and are currently failing pending implementation.

#### 1. Design & Rationale
- **Pure Function Layer (`app/domain/strength.py`)**: Zero imports from FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, or the system clock (per D-20, AC-98).
- **Exact Decimal Arithmetic**: Uses Python `Decimal` throughout. For example, $82.5\text{ kg} \times 3\text{ reps} = 82.5 \times 1.1 = 90.75$ exactly (AC-43).
- **Epley Formula**: $\text{e1RM} = \text{load} \times (1 + \text{reps} / 30)$. When $\text{reps} = 1$, $\text{e1RM} = \text{load}$.
- **Volume**: $\sum (\text{load} \times \text{reps})$ calculated across working sets only.
- **PR Progression**: A working set is a PR if its e1RM is **strictly greater** than the highest e1RM of all earlier working sets of that exercise for that user.

#### 2. Key Edge Cases & Potential Traps
1. **Rep Range Boundary (AC-39)**: Epley is only scientifically reliable for $1 \le \text{reps} \le 12$. If $\text{reps} > 12$ or $\text{reps} < 1$, e1RM must evaluate to `None` with reason `"rep_range"`.
2. **Warm-up Sets (AC-39, AC-40)**: Any set marked `is_warmup = True` must return `None` (reason `"warmup"`) and must **never** count toward volume or PR evaluation.
3. **Baseline Rule (AC-41)**: The very first working set provides the benchmark; it is marked `is_baseline = True` and must **not** be flagged as a PR.
4. **Strict Inequality (AC-41)**: An equal e1RM is not a PR ($\text{e1RM} > \text{best}$, not $\ge$).
5. **Deterministic Ordering (AC-41)**: Sets must be evaluated strictly chronologically by `completed_at` ascending, then `set_number` ascending.

---

1. Executive Summary

Build a full-stack fitness application that combines workout logging and strength analytics with a rule-based diet-plan generator. Users log exercises, sets, repetitions and loads; review strength trends; set dietary preferences; and generate editable 7-day meal plans using foods and recipes from a curated multi-cuisine database. The first release prioritizes correctness, explainability, testability and a clear demonstration over opaque AI.

Primary goal: strength improvement. The system supports training consistency, adequate energy and protein intake, and recovery-aware tracking. It does not promise specific strength or body-composition outcomes and is not a medical nutrition service.

2. Goals, Users, and Scope

Target user

A gym user who wants to record resistance-training sessions, monitor strength progression, and receive practical meal suggestions across multiple cuisines.

MVP scope

Authentication and per-user data isolation.

Exercise library, workout routines, session logging, personal records and estimated 1RM.

Food and recipe catalog with per-serving nutrient values and data-source notes.

Profile-based diet-plan generation for 7 days, with user-selectable meals and substitutions.

Cuisine preferences including multiple selections; dietary restrictions, allergens, budget and preparation-time filters.

Grocery-list generation from selected meals.

Dashboard for strength metrics, workout consistency, planned versus logged nutrition, and adherence.

Unit, API, integration and end-to-end tests; seed data; README; demo workflow.

Out of scope for the first release

Medical diagnosis, treatment plans, eating-disorder management or clinical nutrition advice.

Guaranteed optimal meal plans or guaranteed strength gains.

Automatic wearable integration, barcode scanning, payments, social feeds or complex AI chat.

Real-time nutrition data from multiple third-party providers before the core data model is stable.

4. Non-Functional Requirements

Security: hash passwords with a modern password-hashing library; never store plaintext passwords or secrets in source control.

Authorization: enforce ownership checks in every user-specific API operation, not only in the frontend.

Correctness: use decimal/numeric types for quantities where practical; centralize nutrient and strength calculations.

Reliability: use database transactions for multi-row workout and plan writes.

Performance: paginate history endpoints and add indexes for user_id/date and foreign keys.

Maintainability: keep routers/controllers thin; place rules in service modules and persistence in repositories/models.

Explainability: generated plans must expose the target values, constraints applied, and nutrient data provenance.

Accessibility: labels, keyboard operation, readable chart alternatives and meaningful validation errors.

Privacy: collect only required profile data and provide clear delete/edit controls.

6. Database Schema

Use UUID primary keys, created_at/updated_at timestamps, foreign keys and database constraints. Store timestamps in UTC; store the user's preferred timezone in the profile for daily summaries. The schema below is a logical MVP schema, not a complete SQL migration.

Table

Key fields

Purpose

users

id UUID PK; email UNIQUE; password_hash; created_at; is_active

Account identity and authentication.

user_profiles

user_id UUID PK/FK users; display_name; birth_date optional; height_cm optional; body_weight_kg optional; timezone; units; goal; activity_level optional

User-controlled settings. Avoid collecting unnecessary sensitive data.

user_cuisine_preferences

id UUID PK; user_id FK; cuisine_code; preference_level

Multiple cuisines per user; UNIQUE(user_id, cuisine_code).

user_food_constraints

id UUID PK; user_id FK; constraint_type; constraint_value; is_hard_constraint

187: 7. Core Business Logic

188: Strength analytics

189: Estimated one-rep maximum (Epley approximation): e1RM = load × (1 + reps / 30). Use primarily for sets with a reasonable rep range; label it an estimate, not a measured maximum.

190: Training volume for a set = load × reps. Session volume is the sum across eligible working sets. Show exercise-specific trends and distinguish warm-up sets if users mark them.

191: Nutrition calculations

192: For a nutrient stored per 100 g: nutrient amount = (edible food weight in grams / 100) × nutrient_per_100g. For recipe totals, sum ingredient nutrients, then divide by the recipe's stated servings. Clearly document assumptions for raw versus cooked foods and edible portions.

193: Rule-based plan generation

194: Load the user's active profile, current targets, cuisine preferences, hard restrictions, allergies, budget and preparation-time limits.

195: Filter candidate recipes and foods. Allergens and explicit restrictions are hard exclusions; cuisine preference and variety are ranking preferences.

196: Select meal candidates across the requested number of days, favoring variety and practical preparation.

197: Score candidates using target deviation, preference match, preparation time, budget estimates and repetition penalties.

198: Assemble meals, calculate estimated daily nutrients, and return the plan with per-day totals and warnings when targets cannot be met.

199: Allow edits and substitutions; recalculate affected meals, daily totals and grocery quantities.

200: Persist the selected plan and snapshot the targets and nutrient values used.

201: MVP algorithm: deterministic greedy selection with a scoring function and hard constraints. A later version may use integer/linear programming for stronger optimization. Do not claim that the plan is globally optimal.

202: Target-setting safety

203: The application may provide optional estimate-based targets, but must display the inputs and assumptions, allow manual editing, and avoid prescriptive clinical advice. Do not generate restrictive calorie targets for minors or users who indicate a relevant medical condition without an appropriate professional-guidance flow. Do not present the app as a substitute for a registered dietitian.

204: 8. SDD Specification

205: Create a single repository-level SPEC.md as the source of truth. Keep implementation decisions traceable to requirements and acceptance tests.

213: 3. Personas and user journeys

221: 7. API contract

225: 9. Security and privacy

227: 10. Acceptance criteria

233: Example acceptance criteria

234: Area

235: Given / When / Then

236: Workout logging

237: Given an authenticated user, when they save a workout containing exercises and sets, then the session and all child sets persist and appear in history.

238: Ownership

239: Given user A's workout ID, when user B requests it, then the API returns 404 or 403 and discloses no workout details.

240: Allergen filtering

241: Given a configured hard allergy, when a plan is generated, then no selected recipe or ingredient contains that allergen according to the catalog metadata.

242: Nutrient math

243: Given 150 g of a food containing 20 g protein per 100 g, when totals are calculated, then protein equals 30 g before any documented rounding.

244: Plan target visibility

245: Given a generated plan, when the user views a day, then calorie and macro totals, target values and any target-deviation warnings are visible.

246: Substitution

247: Given a meal substitution, when the replacement is accepted, then nutrient totals and the grocery list recalculate and the plan remains editable.

248: Grocery list

249: Given repeated ingredients across several planned meals, when the grocery list is generated, then compatible units are aggregated and incompatible units are kept separate.

1: # Learning Log
2: 
3: Each step adds an entry: what was built, why it's designed that way, one risk, and 3 quiz questions.
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## Step 1 — Repo, Tooling, and Walking-Skeleton Compose Stack
8: 
9: **What was built:** Project structure with backend (FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + Alembic), frontend (React + Vite + TypeScript), and Docker Compose stack (PostgreSQL, backend, frontend/nginx). Health check endpoint at `/api/health`.
10: 
11: **Why it's designed this way:**
12: - **Modular monolith** (D-01): simpler than microservices but with clean layer boundaries (`domain` → `services` → `repositories` → `api`).
13: - **Async SQLAlchemy**: PostgreSQL with asyncpg for non-blocking database access, important when handling concurrent API requests.
14: - **Non-root containers** (D2): security best practice — if a container is compromised, the attacker has limited privileges.
15: - **Nginx as reverse proxy**: serves the SPA, proxies `/api/` to the backend, and adds security headers (SEC9).
16: 
17: **What could go wrong:** If the Alembic migration runs before PostgreSQL is fully ready, it will fail. That's why Docker Compose uses `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy` and the database has a `pg_isready` health check.
18: 
19: **Quiz questions:**
20: 1. Why do we use `depends_on: condition: service_healthy` instead of just `depends_on`? What would happen without the health check condition?
21: 2. Why does the backend entrypoint run `alembic upgrade head` before starting uvicorn? What happens on the very first deploy vs subsequent deploys?
22: 3. The nginx config has `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html`. Why is this needed for a React SPA, and what would happen without it?

+## Step 2 — Pure Domain Functions (Units, Strength, Nutrients, Targets, Grocery, Scoring)
+
+**What was built:** Pure domain modules in `backend/app/domain/` with zero framework, database, or clock imports:
+- `units.py` (AC-16): Exact `Decimal` mass conversions ($100\text{ lb} = 45.359237\text{ kg}$), round-trip consistency ($< 10^{-9}$), cooking volume units (D-15), and 1-decimal-place display formatting.
+- `targets.py` (AC-19–21): Mifflin–St Jeor BMR, TDEE activity multipliers, +5% strength goal adjustment, macro split defaults ($1.6\text{ g/kg}$ protein, $25\%$ fat, remainder carbs), and energy floor detection ($< 1,500\text{ kcal}$).
+- `scoring.py` (AC-63, AC-64): Candidate target fit deviation, multi-factor scoring formula with weights ($w_t, w_c, w_p, w_b, w_r$), and discrete serving size selection ($0.5$ to $3.0$ with ties going to the smaller size).
+- `strength.py` (AC-39–41, AC-43): Epley e1RM formula (1–12 rep range), warm-up set exclusion, working volume summation, and chronological PR detection (first working set as baseline, strict inequality for PRs).
+- `nutrients.py` (AC-45–47): Per-100g nutrient scaling, edible weight accounting, and recipe totals / per-serving breakdown.
+- `grocery.py` (AC-77–79): Ingredient scaling by planned servings, segregation into incompatible unit families (`mass`, `volume`, `count`), and canonical aggregation with display thresholds ($1,000\text{ g} \to 1.2\text{ kg}$, $1,000\text{ ml} \to 1.5\text{ l}$).
+
+**Why it's designed this way:**
+- **Layering & Pure Functions (D-20, AC-98):** Domain functions do not import FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, or the system clock. They take explicit arguments and return plain values or dataclasses, guaranteeing determinism and lightning-fast test execution without mock databases.
+- **Exact Decimals (D-05, AC-43):** Floating point binary fractions cause subtle arithmetic drift. Using `Decimal` guarantees exact calculations for fitness loads and nutritional targets.
+- **Unit Family Segregation (AC-78):** Aggregating mass and volume requires ingredient density (e.g. 1 cup of flour $\ne$ 1 cup of honey). Without verified density metadata, attempting density conversion would corrupt recipe grocery lists; keeping them separate prevents errors.
+
+**What could go wrong:** If workout sets are not ordered strictly chronologically before evaluating PRs (or if timestamps are null and set numbers are shuffled), a weaker subsequent set could be evaluated before a stronger one, corrupting the personal record progression and misidentifying the baseline set.
+
+**Quiz questions:**
+1. Why is Epley's formula ($e1RM = \text{load} \times (1 + \text{reps} / 30)$) restricted to $1 \le \text{reps} \le 12$, and why is $1\text{ rep}$ treated as an identity ($\text{load}$)?
+2. In recipe nutrition calculations, why must `edible_weight_g` take precedence over purchased `quantity_g`, and how would ignoring this affect bone-in meat or unpeeled vegetables?
+3. Why do we keep grocery quantities in separate unit families (`mass`, `volume`, `count`) rather than converting cups or tablespoons of an ingredient into grams?
+

+def test_ac_11_security_headers_present():
+    """AC-11 (SEC9): Responses carry CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, frame protection."""
+    from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
+    from app.main import app
+
+    client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
+    # Ping /api/health which is open
+    resp = client.get("/api/health")
+
+    headers = resp.headers
+    assert headers.get("X-Content-Type-Options") == "nosniff"
+    assert headers.get("Referrer-Policy") == "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
+    assert headers.get("X-Frame-Options") == "DENY"
+    assert "Content-Security-Policy" in headers
+    assert "default-src 'self'" in headers["Content-Security-Policy"]
+
+
+def test_ac_13_request_body_above_1mb_rejected():
+    """AC-13 (SEC8): Request body above 1 MB returns 413."""
+    from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
+    from app.main import app
+
+    client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
+    # Create payload slightly over 1 MB (1024 * 1024 + 10 bytes)
+    large_payload = "x" * (1024 * 1024 + 10)
+
+    resp = client.post(
+        "/api/auth/register",
+        content=large_payload,
+        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
+    )
+    assert resp.status_code == 413
+    data = resp.json()
+    assert data["error"]["code"] == "body_too_large"
+

+## Step 3 — Database Models, Migrations, Authentication, Sessions, CSRF, and Security (AC-01 to AC-13, AC-15, AC-97, AC-98, AC-104)
+
+**What was built:**
+- Full relational schema in `backend/app/models/` (24 entities: users, sessions, profiles, food constraints, cuisine preferences, exercises, routines, routine_exercises, workout_sessions, workout_exercises, workout_sets, foods, food_nutrients, food_allergens, recipes, recipe_ingredients, recipe_diet_tags, recipe_meal_types, nutrition_goals, meal_plans, planned_meals, planned_meal_items, nutrition_logs, nutrition_log_items).
+- Initial schema Alembic migration: `backend/alembic/versions/001_initial_schema.py`.
+- Argon2id password hashing and constant-time dummy verification for unknown emails (SEC1, SEC5, AC-01–03).
+- Server-side revocable session cookies (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` over TLS) with SHA-256 token hashing (SEC2, AC-03, AC-05).
+- Double-submit CSRF token validation on all state-changing endpoints (SEC3, AC-06).
+- Rate limiter restricting failed logins to 5 attempts per 15 minutes with `Retry-After` (SEC6, AC-04).
+- TLS enforcement returning 403 `tls_required` for remote clients accessing credentials over plain HTTP (SEC7, AC-07).
+- Ownership isolation matrix test harness verifying cross-user access returns 404 identical to non-existent resources (SEC4, AC-08).
+- Strict Pydantic schemas with `extra="forbid"` preventing parameter injection like client-supplied `user_id` (SEC8, AC-09).
+- Middleware enforcing 1 MB request body size limit returning 413 (SEC8, AC-13).
+- Security response headers: CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and restricted CORS (SEC9, AC-11).
+- Profile validation enforcing ranges (height 50–260 cm, weight 20–400 kg) and IANA timezone verification (FR-01, AC-15).
+- Domain purity test ensuring `app/domain` contains zero framework, DB, or clock dependencies (AC-98).
+- Canary logging test verifying no password, token, session ID, or full email address is logged (SEC12, AC-104).
+
+**Why it's designed this way:**
+- **Defense in Depth:** Passwords are never stored in plaintext (Argon2id). Session tokens and CSRF tokens are stored only as SHA-256 digests; even a complete SQL dump yields zero usable session tokens.
+- **Service/Database Layer Ownership:** Ownership authorization is never trusted to client-side filters. Querying by `(id, user_id)` ensures unauthorized accesses result in a uniform 404 Not Found, preventing IDOR attacks and information disclosure.
+- **Constant-Time Verification:** When an email does not exist, verifying a dummy Argon2id hash prevents attackers from measuring server response times to enumerate registered accounts.
+
+**What could go wrong:** If the frontend SPA omits the `X-CSRF-Token` header on mutating POST/PATCH/DELETE calls, requests fail with 403 `csrf_failed`. Additionally, if sessions are stored only in memory without database synchronization, restarting backend servers would invalidate active logins.
+
+**Quiz questions:**
+1. Why do we store only the SHA-256 hash of session and CSRF tokens in the database rather than the raw tokens generated by `secrets.token_urlsafe`?
+2. How does checking a dummy password hash on unknown emails prevent timing side-channel attacks during login?
+3. Why must ownership checks return 404 Not Found rather than 403 Forbidden when a user accesses a resource belonging to someone else?
+
+

1: # SPEC.md: Gym Workout Logger and Strength-Focused Diet Planner

2: 

3: **Version:** 1.0 (draft, based on *Advanced Gym Workout Logger + Strength-Focused Diet Planner: Updated Project Blueprint*)

4: **Last updated:** 2026-10-16

5: **Methodology:** Spec-Driven Development. Every requirement has an ID, and every acceptance criterion (AC) becomes at least one automated test or one recorded measurement.

6: 

7: > Numbers marked *initial* (thresholds, weights, targets) are starting values. If you change one after measuring, record the change in the Decisions Log (section 18). Safety thresholds in section 3 are placeholders for you to review against a qualified source and cite in the README; they are not professional advice.

8: 

9: ---

10: 

11: ## 1. Overview

12: 

13: A full-stack web application that combines two things in one place: a **workout logger** with strength analytics (sets, reps, load, estimated one-rep max, personal records, volume, consistency) and a **rule-based diet-plan generator** that builds editable 7-day, multi-cuisine meal plans from a reviewed food and recipe catalogue, with substitutions, a grocery list, and a way to log what you actually ate.

14: 

15: The first release favours **correctness, explainability and testability over opaque AI**. Every number the app shows can be traced to a formula, a catalogue value with a recorded source, or a setting the user chose. The planner is a deterministic scorer with hard safety filters (allergies first), not a promise of an optimal plan, and the app is informational, not medical nutrition advice and not a promise of strength gains.

16: 

17: ### Aim

18: 

19: Build a secure, well-tested full-stack application that lets a gym user record training, see honest strength trends, and generate and adjust meal plans that respect their allergies and preferences, with clear explanations, protective safety rules, and a deployment you can open in a browser on your computer or local network.

20: 

21: ### Inputs

22: 

23: | Input | Details |

24: | --- | --- |

25: | Account and profile | Email, password, display name, timezone, units (kg or lb), optional height, weight and birth date, activity level, goal, and wellbeing settings (section 3) |

26: | Training data | Exercises, routines, sessions and sets (reps, load, optional RPE, rest, warm-up flag) |

27: | Nutrition preferences | Cuisines (several, with a preference level), diet tags, allergies, excluded ingredients, budget, preparation-time limit, target calories and macros |

28: | Meal plan actions | Generate, edit servings, substitute, accept or reject suggestions |

29: | Intake logs | What the user actually ate, by food or recipe and quantity |

30: | Seed catalogue | Reviewed exercises, foods with nutrient values and provenance, and recipes (section 4) |

31: | Configuration | Environment variables: database URL, secrets, allowed origin, registration switch, demo mode |

32: 

33: ### Outputs

34: 

35: | Output | Details |

36: | --- | --- |

37: | Workout history and strength analytics | Per-exercise estimated 1RM, personal records, volume and trends, with every estimate labelled |

38: | Nutrition targets | Editable targets, with the inputs and assumptions that produced any estimate |

39: | Meal plans | 7-day plans with per-meal and per-day nutrient totals, warnings, and an explanation of the filters and scoring used |

40: | Substitution options | Eligible alternatives with nutrient differences |

41: | Grocery list | Aggregated ingredients across chosen days, with units kept consistent |

42: | Dashboard and insights | Consistency, strength trends, planned versus logged nutrition, and explainable observations with their time window, sample size and limitations |

43: | Data export | A complete JSON export of the user's data, and verified account deletion |

44: | Deployed service | The web application, running in containers at `http://localhost:8080` (and over HTTPS on the local network) |

45: 

46: ### Requirements at a glance

47: 

48: - **Functional:** FR-01 to FR-20 (section 12), including the blueprint's FR-01 to FR-15.

49: - **Safety, wellbeing and privacy:** S1 to S10 (section 3).

50: - **Data rules:** DL1 to DL4 (section 4).

51: - **Security:** section 10. **Deployment:** D1 to D8 (section 11).

52: - **Non-functional:** section 15.

53: - **Acceptance criteria:** AC-01 to AC-118 (section 13), mapped to the blueprint's requirements in section 14.

54: 

55: ## 2. Goals, Scope and Non-Goals

56: 

57: **Goals**

58: 1. Accounts with strict per-user data isolation.

59: 2. An exercise catalogue, routines, session and set logging, personal records, estimated 1RM and volume.

60: 3. A reviewed food and recipe catalogue with nutrient values and provenance.

61: 4. Nutrition profile, editable targets, and protective safety rules.

62: 5. A deterministic, explainable, editable 7-day plan generator with allergy-first filtering.

63: 6. Substitutions with recalculated totals, and a unit-aware grocery list.

64: 7. Intake logging, and planned versus actual comparison.

65: 8. A dashboard and descriptive insights that avoid causal claims.

66: 9. Export and deletion of user data.

67: 10. A tested, documented, deployed system.

68: 

69: **Non-goals (v1)**

70: - Medical diagnosis, treatment plans, eating-disorder management or clinical nutrition advice.

71: - Weight-loss or calorie-deficit goals (decision D-11); supported goals are `maintain` and `build_strength`.

72: - Guaranteed optimal plans or guaranteed strength gains.

73: - Wearable integration, barcode scanning, payments, social features, AI chat, and real-time nutrition data from third-party providers.

74: - Email verification, password reset and social login (documented limitations).

75: 

76: **Stretch** (only after every required criterion passes): an integer-programming planner, a nutrition-and-strength association insight (with strong guardrails), rest timers, a custom-food editor, idempotency keys for workout creation, and a public demo deployment.

77: 

78: ## 3. Safety, Wellbeing and Privacy Rules

79: 

80: This app touches food, body data and health-adjacent decisions, so these rules are requirements, not polish.

81: 

82: | ID | Rule |

83: | --- | --- |

84: | **S1 Informational notice** | Every target, plan, log summary and insight screen, and every plan API response, carries a notice that estimates are informational and not medical advice, and that the app is not a substitute for a registered dietitian or doctor. |

85: | **S2 Adults only for nutrition planning** | Nutrition targets, plan generation and estimates require the user to confirm they are 18 or older (`adult_confirmed_at`). If a birth date is given and shows the user is under 18, nutrition planning and estimates are disabled for that account (`nutrition_not_available_for_minors`), with a message recommending guidance from a parent or guardian and a qualified professional. Workout logging and strength analytics stay available. The confirmation is self-declared, which is a documented limitation. |

86: | **S3 Professional-guidance flag** | A profile flag `needs_professional_guidance` (a yes or no only; no condition details are collected) disables estimate-based targets. Targets must then be entered manually, with a banner saying to follow the guidance of the user's professional. |

87: | **S4 Estimated targets are optional and transparent** | Estimates use the Mifflin–St Jeor equation, an activity factor and a goal adjustment (section 5.4), and always display their inputs, formula and assumptions. The user can ignore and edit them. |

88: | **S5 Energy floor** | The app never *suggests* an estimated target below `estimate_floor_kcal` (*initial*: 1,500 kcal); it reports `estimate_below_floor` and asks the user to enter a target manually or seek guidance. A manual target below that value is saved with a warning. Plan generation is **refused** below `plan_minimum_kcal` (*initial*: 1,200 kcal). Review both numbers against a qualified source and cite it in the README. |

89: | **S6 No deficit goals** | There is no weight-loss goal, no deficit calculation and no "calories to lose" language in v1. |

90: | **S7 Wellbeing settings** | The user can (a) **hide calorie numbers** everywhere in the UI (macros such as protein stay visible; the planner still uses calories internally), (b) **pause nutrition** (nutrition features are switched off, training continues, data is kept), and (c) track body weight only by **opting in**: no weight is requested or charted by default, and nothing requires it except the optional estimate, which asks at the moment of use. |

91: | **S8 Neutral language** | Nutrition feedback is descriptive, not judgemental: "within your range" and "below your range", never "failed", "cheated", "bad", "guilt" or streak-loss messaging. A test scans UI strings for a banned word list. |

92: | **S9 Allergy handling** | Allergies and explicit exclusions are hard filters. Catalogue data can be incomplete, so items with unknown or unverified allergen status are excluded when the user has any allergy (setting `exclude_unverified_allergens`, default on), and every plan carries a reminder to check labels. |

93: | **S10 Privacy** | Collect only what is needed. Birth date, height, weight and sex-for-estimate are all optional. Logs never contain passwords, tokens or full email addresses. Users can export and delete everything (FR-15). |

94: 

95: ## 4. Data Rules and Licences

96: 

97: | ID | Rule |

98: | --- | --- |

99: | **DL1 Recorded sources** | Every food has `data_source`, a `source_reference` where possible, a serving basis, a raw or cooked state, and a `verified_at` date. Values that are estimates or imputed are flagged `approximate` and labelled that way in the API and UI. |

100: | **DL2 Licensed data only** | Nutrient data comes from sources whose licence permits this use, recorded in `DATA_LICENCES.md`. Government composition tables such as USDA FoodData Central are commonly public domain, but check each source and each table's licence yourself; if a licence is unclear, do not use the data. |

279: ## 8. Architecture

280: 

281: A **modular monolith** (decision D-01): simpler to build, test and explain than microservices, with clear module boundaries.

282: 

283: | Layer | Contents | Rule |

284: | --- | --- | --- |

285: | Routers (`app/api`) | FastAPI routers, dependencies, Pydantic schemas | Thin: parse, authorise, call a service, return |

286: | Services (`app/services`) | WorkoutService, StrengthAnalyticsService, NutritionService, PlanGeneratorService, GroceryListService, InsightService | Orchestrate use cases and transactions |

287: | Domain (`app/domain`) | Pure functions: units, e1RM, volume, PR detection, nutrient maths, targets, candidate filters, scoring, aggregation | No framework, database or clock imports; deterministic |

288: | Persistence (`app/models`, `app/repositories`) | SQLAlchemy models, repositories, Alembic migrations | All queries scoped by the authenticated user |

289: | Seed (`app/seed`) | Catalogue importers and validators | Idempotent |

290: | Frontend (`frontend/src`) | React and TypeScript pages, forms, charts | Types generated from the API's OpenAPI document (decision D-17) |

291: 

292: The blueprint's repository layout is kept (`backend/`, `frontend/`, `SPEC.md`, `README.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `.env.example`, `docker-compose.yml`), with `docs/` for the ER diagram, architecture diagram, `DATA_LICENCES.md` and `test-plan.md`.

293: 

294: ## 9. UI Requirements

295: 

296: | Screen | Contents |

297: | --- | --- |

298: | Sign in and register | Validation messages, rate-limit message |

299: | Profile and settings | Profile, units, timezone, wellbeing settings (S7), adult confirmation, professional-guidance flag, data export and deletion |

300: | Exercises | Search, filters, custom exercises |

301: | Routines | Create, edit, duplicate, start |

302: | Workout logger | Active session with fast set entry (a new set copies the previous set's values), warm-up toggle, RPE, notes |

303: | History | Paginated sessions with details |

304: | Strength | Per-exercise e1RM trend, PRs, volume, with a data-table alternative to each chart |

305: | Nutrition preferences and targets | Cuisines, diet tags, allergies, exclusions, limits, targets with assumptions |

306: | Plan | A 7-day grid, day detail with totals, target values and warnings, the explanation panel |

307: | Substitution | Suggested alternatives with nutrient differences |

308: | Grocery list | Grouped checklist |

309: | Nutrition log | Add and edit what was eaten |

310: | Dashboard | Consistency, strength, planned versus logged, insights with their limitations |

311: 

312: Every screen has **loading, empty and error states**. Forms show field-level errors linked to their fields with `aria-describedby`. All controls work by keyboard with a visible focus. The layout works at 360 pixels wide, because the logger is used in the gym. Colour is never the only carrier of meaning, and charts have a text or table alternative.

314: ## 10. Security

315: 

316: | ID | Requirement |

317: | --- | --- |

318: | **SEC1 Passwords** | Hashed with **Argon2id**; minimum 12 and maximum 128 characters; plaintext never stored, logged or returned. |

319: | **SEC2 Sessions** | Server-side, revocable sessions in an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie that is `Secure` whenever served over TLS; logout and account deletion revoke them. |

320: | **SEC3 CSRF** | Every non-GET request must carry a CSRF token (double-submit) or fail with `csrf_failed`. |

321: | **SEC4 Authorisation** | Ownership is enforced in every service and repository call, never only in the UI. Foreign resources return 404. |

322: | **SEC5 Authentication errors** | A wrong email and a wrong password give the identical response. A dummy hash is checked for unknown emails so timing does not reveal them. |

323: | **SEC6 Rate limiting** | At most 5 failed logins per account and per IP in 15 minutes, then 429 with `Retry-After`. |

324: | **SEC7 TLS for credentials** | Credentials are accepted from non-localhost clients only over TLS (`tls_required`). Forwarded-protocol headers are trusted only from the configured reverse proxy. |

325: | **SEC8 Input validation** | Strict schemas, forbidden extra fields, range checks, a 1 MB body limit, and parameterised queries only. |

326: | **SEC9 Headers and CORS** | A Content-Security-Policy, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, frame protection, and CORS limited to the configured origin. |

327: | **SEC10 Secrets** | Only in environment variables; `.env` is never committed; the application refuses to start in production mode with missing or placeholder secrets. |

328: | **SEC11 Dependencies** | `pip-audit` and `npm audit` are run before release and their results recorded. |

329: | **SEC12 Logging** | Structured logs with request IDs; no passwords, tokens, session IDs or full email addresses. |

330: 

331: ## 11. Production Deployment

332: 

333: The project must run as a deployed service. "Deployed" means: built into container images and run as long-lived services that you open in a browser on your own computer or from another device on the same network (intranet). It stores personal fitness and food data, so credentials and sessions must not cross a network in the clear.

334: 

335: | ID | Requirement |

336: | --- | --- |

337: | **D1 Services** | Docker Compose runs `db` (PostgreSQL with a named volume), `backend` (FastAPI under a production server, not auto-reload), and `frontend` (the built React files served by nginx, which proxies `/api` to the backend). |

338: | **D2 Non-root, pinned** | Application containers run as a non-root user; base images and dependencies are pinned. |

339: | **D3 One command** | After `cp .env.example .env` and setting the secrets, `docker compose up -d` builds and starts everything, applies migrations, and serves the UI at `http://localhost:8080`. |

340: | **D4 Seed and demo data** | `docker compose run --rm backend python -m app.seed` loads the reviewed catalogue; `python -m app.demo_user` creates a clearly labelled **synthetic** demo account with 12 weeks of workouts and nutrition logs for the demonstration. |

341: | **D5 Health and restart** | `/api/health` reports the database status; all services have health checks and `restart: unless-stopped`. |

342: | **D6 HTTPS on the network** | For use from other devices, a TLS reverse proxy (for example Caddy or nginx) serves `https://<LAN-IP>:8443`, using a certificate from a private certificate authority you create (a tool such as mkcert can do this) that your devices trust. Plain-HTTP credentials from non-localhost clients are refused (SEC7). |

343: | **D7 Backups** | A documented `pg_dump` backup and restore procedure, verified by restoring into a clean database. |

344: | **D8 Optional public host** | A public deployment on a free host is optional and must run with registration limited and only synthetic data. |

371: ## 13. Acceptance Criteria

372: 

373: Dates and clocks in tests are injected, so results are deterministic.

374: 

375: ### Accounts and security

376: - [ ] **AC-01** (SEC1) Registering stores an Argon2id hash (the stored value starts with `$argon2id$`), never returns or logs the password, and returns 409 `email_taken` for a duplicate email, compared case-insensitively (`A@x.com` and `a@x.com` conflict).

377: - [ ] **AC-02** (SEC1) A password of 11 characters is rejected with 422; 12 and 128 characters are accepted; 129 is rejected.

378: - [ ] **AC-03** (SEC2, SEC5) Login sets an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie (and `Secure` over TLS); a wrong email and a wrong password return the same status and body (`invalid_credentials`).

379: - [ ] **AC-04** (SEC6) The 6th failed login within 15 minutes for one account returns 429 with `Retry-After`; after the window passes (injected clock) a correct login succeeds.

380: - [ ] **AC-05** (SEC2) After logout, the old session cookie returns 401 on every endpoint.

381: - [ ] **AC-06** (SEC3) A POST, PATCH or DELETE without a valid CSRF token returns 403 `csrf_failed`; GET requests are unaffected.

382: - [ ] **AC-07** (SEC7) A login over plain HTTP from a non-localhost client returns 403 `tls_required`; over TLS, or from localhost, it works; a forged forwarded-protocol header from an untrusted client is ignored.

383: - [ ] **AC-08** (SEC4) *Ownership matrix.* For every user-owned endpoint (derived automatically from the route table), user B requesting, changing or deleting user A's resource by ID gets a 404 identical to a missing ID, list endpoints never include A's items, and A's data is unchanged in the database.

384: - [ ] **AC-09** (SEC8) A request body containing `user_id` (or any unknown field) is rejected with 422.

385: - [ ] **AC-10** (SEC8) The string `'; DROP TABLE users;--` saved in a note is stored and returned literally, and all tables remain intact.

386: - [ ] **AC-11** (SEC9) Responses carry the Content-Security-Policy, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy` and frame-protection headers; CORS allows only the configured origin.

387: - [ ] **AC-12** (SEC10) A script finds no secret patterns in tracked files and no tracked `.env`; in production mode the application refuses to start with a missing secret or one equal to the `.env.example` placeholder.

388: - [ ] **AC-13** (SEC8) A request body above 1 MB returns 413.

389: - [ ] **AC-14** (SEC11) `pip-audit` and `npm audit` show no known high or critical vulnerabilities at release; the results are recorded.

395: - [ ] **AC-18** (S3) With `needs_professional_guidance` on, the estimate endpoint returns 409 `manual_targets_required`, manual targets are accepted, and responses carry `requires_professional_guidance: true`.

396: - [ ] **AC-19** (S4) For male, 80 kg, 180 cm, age 25, moderate activity, `build_strength`: BMR 1,805, TDEE 2,797.75, plus 5% = 2,937.64, rounded to **2,940 kcal**; protein **128 g** (1.6 × 80); fat **82 g** (25% of 2,940 kcal ÷ 9); carbohydrate **423 g** (the remaining 1,693 kcal ÷ 4). The response lists the formula, activity factor, goal adjustment, protein and fat assumptions.

397: - [ ] **AC-20** (S4) The same inputs with `sex_for_estimate = unspecified` use `s = −78`: BMR 1,722, TDEE 2,669.1, plus 5% = 2,802.56, rounded to **2,800 kcal**, and the assumption is shown.

398: - [ ] **AC-21** (S5) For female, 45 kg, 160 cm, age 30, sedentary, `maintain` (BMR 1,139, TDEE 1,366.8), the estimate endpoint returns `estimate_below_floor`, saves no target, and tells the user to enter a target manually or seek guidance.

399: - [ ] **AC-22** (S5) A manual target of 1,400 kcal is saved with a `below_recommended_minimum` warning; a manual target of 1,100 kcal is saved, but plan generation returns 422 `target_below_minimum`.

407: ### Exercises, workouts and routines

408: - [ ] **AC-29** (FR-02) Searching `squat` returns exercises whose name contains it (case-insensitive), filters by muscle and equipment work, results are paginated, and a custom exercise is visible only to its owner.

409: - [ ] **AC-30** (FR-02) A custom exercise name must be unique per owner (case-insensitive), otherwise 409; seed exercises cannot be edited or deleted by users.

410: - [ ] **AC-31** (FR-03) Saving a workout with exercises and sets persists the session and every child row, and it appears in history in the saved order.

411: - [ ] **AC-32** (FR-03) Validation: reps 0 and load −1 are rejected; load 0 is accepted; RPE 11 is rejected, 7.5 accepted, and 7.3 rejected (steps of 0.5); duplicate set numbers are rejected; a set `completed_at` earlier than the session start is rejected.

412: - [ ] **AC-33** (NFR) *Atomicity.* A workout with three valid sets and one invalid set returns 422 and leaves no session, exercise or set rows; an injected database failure midway rolls everything back.

413: - [ ] **AC-34** (FR-15) Editing a workout replaces its sets and analytics update; deleting it removes its children and no other user's data.

414: - [ ] **AC-35** (FR-04) A routine stores ordered exercises with target sets and rep ranges (`rep_min ≤ rep_max`); duplicating it makes an independent copy; starting a workout from it pre-fills exercises and targets with no sets logged and records the `routine_id`.

415: - [ ] **AC-36** (5.1) For `Asia/Kolkata`, sets at `2026-10-15T18:29:59Z` and `2026-10-15T18:30:00Z` fall on 15 October and 16 October (local) respectively, and per-day counts follow.

416: - [ ] **AC-37** (7) History pagination returns at most `limit` items in a stable order, and `next_cursor` continues without duplicates or gaps even when new sessions are inserted between page requests.

417: - [ ] **AC-38** (NFR) With 10,000 sessions, the history query plan uses the `(user_id, started_at)` index.

428: - [ ] **AC-45** (FR-09) 150 g of a food with 20 g protein per 100 g gives exactly 30 g protein.

429: - [ ] **AC-46** (5.3) An ingredient of 200 g with `edible_weight_g` 150 uses 150 g in the calculation.

440: ### Plan generation

441: - [ ] **AC-56** (5.5) The same inputs and catalogue give identical plans (compared on content), over 20 runs.

442: - [ ] **AC-57** (S9) *Allergen property test.* For each of the 14 allergens and 100 random preference sets, a generated plan contains no recipe or ingredient carrying that allergen.

443: - [ ] **AC-58** (S9) With any allergy set and `exclude_unverified_allergens` on, no plan includes a recipe with a text-only ingredient or an ingredient with unverified allergen data.

444: - [ ] **AC-59** (5.5) A vegan user's plan contains only vegan recipes; the same holds for each diet tag; an excluded ingredient never appears (case-insensitive, by name and by food).

446: - [ ] **AC-61** (5.5) With preferred cuisines set and enough candidates, at least 70% of planned meals (*initial*) come from preferred cuisines; if only "avoid" cuisines can fill a slot, the plan is still produced with a `cuisine_preference_unmet` warning.

450: - [ ] **AC-65** (5.5) Candidates with equal scores are ordered by recipe ID ascending, identically across runs.

1: # Data Licences
2: 
3: Every food nutrient value in the seed catalogue must come from a source whose licence permits this use. This file records each source.
4: 
5: ## Sources
6: 
7: ### 1. USDA FoodData Central (SR Legacy / Foundation Foods)
8: 
9: - **Publisher:** U.S. Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service
10: - **URL:** https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/
11: - **Licence:** Public domain (U.S. government work, not subject to copyright)
12: - **Used for:** Nutrient values for common Western foods (chicken, rice, eggs, vegetables, etc.)
13: - **Access date:** TBD (will be recorded when seed data is created in Step 4)
14: 
15: ### 2. Indian Food Composition Tables (IFCT) — NIN/ICMR
16:

1: """Nutrient scaling and recipe total domain functions.
2: 
3: Pure functions only — no framework, database, or clock imports (D-20, AC-98).
4: All calculations use exact Decimals (D-05, AC-43).
5: Implements per-100g nutrient scaling, edible weight accounting, and recipe totals /
6: per-serving partitioning (spec §5.3, AC-45–47).
7: """
8: 
9: from collections.abc import Iterable
10: from dataclasses import dataclass
11: from decimal import Decimal
12: 
13: 
14: @dataclass(frozen=True)
15: class NutrientProfile:
16:     """Nutrient amounts, either per 100g or as a scaled total."""
17: 
18:     calories: Decimal
19:     protein_g: Decimal
20:     carbs_g: Decimal
21:     fat_g: Decimal
22:     fiber_g: Decimal = Decimal("0")
23: 
24:     def __add__(self, other: "NutrientProfile") -> "NutrientProfile":
25:         return NutrientProfile(
26:             calories=self.calories + other.calories,
27:             protein_g=self.protein_g + other.protein_g,
28:             carbs_g=self.carbs_g + other.carbs_g,
29:             fat_g=self.fat_g + other.fat_g,
30:             fiber_g=self.fiber_g + other.fiber_g,
31:         )
32: 
33:     def divide(self, divisor: Decimal) -> "NutrientProfile":
34:         if divisor <= Decimal("0"):
35:             raise ValueError("Divisor must be strictly positive")
36:         return NutrientProfile(
37:             calories=self.calories / divisor,
38:             protein_g=self.protein_g / divisor,
39:             carbs_g=self.carbs_g / divisor,
40:             fat_g=self.fat_g / divisor,
41:             fiber_g=self.fiber_g / divisor,
42:         )
43: 
44: 
45: @dataclass(frozen=True)
46: class RecipeIngredientInput:
47:     """Input for an ingredient in a recipe nutrient calculation."""
48: 
49:     food_nutrients: NutrientProfile
50:     quantity_g: Decimal
51:     edible_weight_g: Decimal | None = None
52: 
53: 
54: @dataclass(frozen=True)
55: class RecipeNutrientResult:
56:     """Calculated total and per-serving nutrient totals for a recipe."""
57: 
58:     total: NutrientProfile
59:     per_serving: NutrientProfile
60: 
61: 
62: def calculate_food_nutrients(
63:     weight_g: Decimal,
64:     per_100g: NutrientProfile,
65: ) -> NutrientProfile:
66:     """Calculate nutrients for an edible weight of food in grams (spec §5.3, AC-45).
67: 
68:     Formula: nutrient = (edible weight in g / 100) × nutrient per 100 g.
69:     """
70:     factor = weight_g / Decimal("100")
71:     return NutrientProfile(
72:         calories=factor * per_100g.calories,
73:         protein_g=factor * per_100g.protein_g,
74:         carbs_g=factor * per_100g.carbs_g,
75:         fat_g=factor * per_100g.fat_g,
76:         fiber_g=factor * per_100g.fiber_g,
77:     )
78: 
79: 
80: def calculate_recipe_nutrients(
81:     ingredients: Iterable[RecipeIngredientInput],
82:     servings: Decimal,
83: ) -> RecipeNutrientResult:
84:     """Calculate recipe total and per-serving nutrient amounts (spec §5.3, AC-46, AC-47).
85: 
86:     Rules:
87:     - If edible_weight_g is provided, it is used instead of purchased quantity_g (AC-46).
88:     - Per-serving nutrients are the sum over ingredients divided by recipe servings (AC-47).
89:     """
90:     if servings <= Decimal("0"):
91:         raise ValueError("Servings must be strictly positive")
92: 
93:     running_total = NutrientProfile(
94:         calories=Decimal("0"),
95:         protein_g=Decimal("0"),
96:         carbs_g=Decimal("0"),
97:         fat_g=Decimal("0"),
98:         fiber_g=Decimal("0"),
99:     )

+def check_atwater_consistency(
+    energy_kcal: Decimal,
+    protein_g: Decimal,
+    carbs_g: Decimal,
+    fat_g: Decimal,
+) -> bool:
+    """Validate 4-4-9 Atwater energy balance rule (spec §4, DL1, AC-50).
+
+    Condition: |kcal - (4*P + 4*C + 9*F)| <= max(20, 0.15 * kcal).
+    """
+    macro_energy = (
+        Decimal("4") * protein_g + Decimal("4") * carbs_g + Decimal("9") * fat_g
+    )
+    diff = abs(energy_kcal - macro_energy)
+    max_tolerance = max(Decimal("20"), Decimal("0.15") * energy_kcal)
+    return diff <= max_tolerance
+

6: AC-47 (5.3): Fixture recipe:
7:     F1 (per 100 g): 150 kcal, 25 g protein, 0 g carbohydrate, 5 g fat.
8:     F2 (per 100 g): 350 kcal, 8 g protein, 75 g carbohydrate, 1 g fat.
9:     Recipe with 200 g F1 and 100 g F2 for 2 servings totals:
10:     650 kcal, 58 g protein, 75 g carbohydrate, 11 g fat.
11:     Per serving: 325 kcal, 29 g protein, 37.5 g carbohydrate, 5.5 g fat.

+    token_hash = hash_token(raw_token)
+    now = datetime.now(UTC)
+    stmt = (
+        select(Session)

+            Session.revoked_at.is_(None),
+            Session.expires_at > now,
+        )
+    )
+    result = await db.execute(stmt)
+    session = result.scalar_one_or_none()
+    if not session or not session.user or not session.user.is_active:

+    return session.user

50: ## Step 3 — Database Models, Migrations, Authentication, Sessions, CSRF, and Security (AC-01 to AC-13, AC-15, AC-97, AC-98, AC-104)
51: 
52: **What was built:**
53: - Full relational schema in `backend/app/models/` (24 entities: users, sessions, profiles, food constraints, cuisine preferences, exercises, routines, routine_exercises, workout_sessions, workout_exercises, workout_sets, foods, food_nutrients, food_allergens, recipes, recipe_ingredients, recipe_diet_tags, recipe_meal_types, nutrition_goals, meal_plans, planned_meals, planned_meal_items, nutrition_logs, nutrition_log_items).
54: - Initial schema Alembic migration: `backend/alembic/versions/001_initial_schema.py`.
55: - Argon2id password hashing and constant-time dummy verification for unknown emails (SEC1, SEC5, AC-01–03).
56: - Server-side revocable session cookies (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` over TLS) with SHA-256 token hashing (SEC2, AC-03, AC-05).
57: - Double-submit CSRF token validation on all state-changing endpoints (SEC3, AC-06).
58: - Rate limiter restricting failed logins to 5 attempts per 15 minutes with `Retry-After` (SEC6, AC-04).
59: - TLS enforcement returning 403 `tls_required` for remote clients accessing credentials over plain HTTP (SEC7, AC-07).
60: - Ownership isolation matrix test harness verifying cross-user access returns 404 identical to non-existent resources (SEC4, AC-08).
61: - Strict Pydantic schemas with `extra="forbid"` preventing parameter injection like client-supplied `user_id` (SEC8, AC-09).
62: - Middleware enforcing 1 MB request body size limit returning 413 (SEC8, AC-13).
63: - Security response headers: CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and restricted CORS (SEC9, AC-11).
64: - Profile validation enforcing ranges (height 50–260 cm, weight 20–400 kg) and IANA timezone verification (FR-01, AC-15).
65: - Domain purity test ensuring `app/domain` contains zero framework, DB, or clock dependencies (AC-98).
66: - Canary logging test verifying no password, token, session ID, or full email address is logged (SEC12, AC-104).
67: 
68: **Why it's designed this way:**
69: - **Defense in Depth:** Passwords are never stored in plaintext (Argon2id). Session tokens and CSRF tokens are stored only as SHA-256 digests; even a complete SQL dump yields zero usable session tokens.
70: - **Service/Database Layer Ownership:** Ownership authorization is never trusted to client-side filters. Querying by `(id, user_id)` ensures unauthorized accesses result in a uniform 404 Not Found, preventing IDOR attacks and information disclosure.
71: - **Constant-Time Verification:** When an email does not exist, verifying a dummy Argon2id hash prevents attackers from measuring server response times to enumerate registered accounts.
72: 
73: **What could go wrong:** If the frontend SPA omits the `X-CSRF-Token` header on mutating POST/PATCH/DELETE calls, requests fail with 403 `csrf_failed`. Additionally, if sessions are stored only in memory without database synchronization, restarting backend servers would invalidate active logins.
74: 
75: **Quiz questions:**
76: 1. Why do we store only the SHA-256 hash of session and CSRF tokens in the database rather than the raw tokens generated by `secrets.token_urlsafe`?
77: 2. How does checking a dummy password hash on unknown emails prevent timing side-channel attacks during login?
78: 3. Why must ownership checks return 404 Not Found rather than 403 Forbidden when a user accesses a resource belonging to someone else?

+## Step 4 — Catalogue Data, Provenance Validation, Atwater Checks, Idempotent Seeding, and Catalogue APIs (AC-48 to AC-55)
+
+**What was built:**
+- Curated seed catalogues in `backend/app/seed/data/`:
+  - `exercises.json`: 35 exercises spanning all 7 primary movement patterns and muscle groups (chest, back, shoulders, quads, hamstrings, glutes, biceps, triceps, core).
+  - `foods.json`: 48 whole and staple foods with full provenance (USDA FoodData Central FDC IDs, Indian IFCT codes), serving descriptions, raw/cooked states, and verification dates.
+  - `recipes.json`: 20 high-protein recipes spanning 4 distinct cuisines (Indian, Italian, Mexican, American/East Asian), with at least 2 ingredients each, positive servings, and prep/cook times.
+- Idempotent seed loader in `backend/app/seed/loader.py`:
+  - Provenance validation checking `data_source`, `serving_description`, `state`, and `verified_at` (DL1, AC-49).
+  - Pure domain Atwater 4-4-9 energy balance validation: $| \text{kcal} - (4P + 4C + 9F) | \le \max(20, 0.15 \times \text{kcal})$ (AC-50).
+  - Recipe allergen union computation and incomplete allergen flagging on text-only ingredients (S9, AC-52).
+  - Idempotent database loading: re-running the seed command produces 0 new inserts and preserves all counts (AC-51).
+  - CLI runner `python -m app.seed` (D4, AC-106).
+- Catalogue API endpoints in `backend/app/api/catalogue.py`:
+  - `GET /api/exercises`: substring search (`q`), muscle and equipment filters, and pagination (AC-29).
+  - `POST /api/exercises`: custom exercise creation with per-user case-insensitive uniqueness check (AC-30).
+  - `GET /api/foods`: search by name and category with clear `is_approximate` labelling (AC-49, AC-53).
+  - `DELETE /api/foods/{id}`: returns 409 Conflict if food is referenced in recipes, plans, or intake history (AC-55).
+  - `GET /api/recipes`: filtering by cuisine, diet tag, meal type, and max total time, with per-serving nutrition dynamically computed using domain functions and complete allergen unions (AC-53).
+- Database check constraints verifying non-negative nutrient amounts, positive servings, and positive ingredient quantities (AC-48).
+- Immutable historical snapshots: `nutrient_snapshot` JSON preservation in `PlannedMealItem` and `NutritionLogItem` (AC-54).
+
+**Why it's designed this way:**
+- **Atwater Energy Consistency:** Bogus nutritional numbers (e.g., claiming 500 kcal for 10g protein and 0g carbs/fat) break target fit scoring in the diet planner. Validating energy against macronutrients ensures catalogue integrity.
+- **Strict Allergen Unions:** A recipe's allergen list is computed directly from its resolved ingredient foods. When an ingredient is text-only (not mapped to a verified food item), the recipe is explicitly flagged with `has_incomplete_allergen_data = true`, enabling the planner's safety filters (S9) to exclude unverified meals for allergic users.
+- **Historical Snapshot Invariance:** In nutrition logging, if a catalogue food's nutritional profile is updated months later, historical logs must reflect what was recorded on that day. Storing a frozen `nutrient_snapshot` prevents retroactive data drift.
+- **Referential Integrity on Deletes:** Foreign keys configured with `ondelete="RESTRICT"` and API-level pre-checks ensure that deleting a catalogue item never cascades into destroying historical workout logs, meal plans, or recipes.
+
+**What could go wrong:**
+- If an ingredient in a recipe is deleted or renamed without maintaining foreign key restrictions, the recipe's nutrient calculations could crash with null references.
+- If Atwater tolerances are set too stringently without accounting for dietary fiber or natural analytical variance, genuine whole foods from official tables (like legumes with 8g+ fiber per 100g) could be rejected during seeding.
+
+**Quiz questions:**
+1. What is the 4-4-9 Atwater energy balance equation, and why is an absolute and percentage tolerance ($\max(20\text{ kcal}, 15\%)$) necessary when validating real food composition data?
+2. Why do historical intake logs and meal plans store a frozen JSON `nutrient_snapshot` rather than simply joining against the `foods` table on every query?
+3. How does the system handle allergen safety when a recipe contains text-only ingredients (i.e. ingredients not linked to a verified food item)?

+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_ac_08_api_ownership_matrix():
+    """AC-08 (SEC4): User B accessing, updating, or deleting User A's routine or workout gets 404."""
+    from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
+    from httpx import ASGITransport, AsyncClient

+    from app.models.workout import Exercise, WorkoutExercise, WorkoutRoutine, WorkoutSession, WorkoutSet
+    from app.services.security import generate_csrf_token, generate_session_token, hash_token
+
+    engine = create_async_engine("sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:", echo=False)
+    async with engine.begin() as conn:
+        await conn.run_sync(Base.metadata.create_all)
+

+        # Create User A
+        user_a = User(email="usera@example.com", password_hash="$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=4$dummy")
+        # Create User B

1: # SPEC.md: Gym Workout Logger and Strength-Focused Diet Planner

2: 

3: **Version:** 1.0 (draft, based on *Advanced Gym Workout Logger + Strength-Focused Diet Planner: Updated Project Blueprint*)

4: **Last updated:** 2026-10-16

5: **Methodology:** Spec-Driven Development. Every requirement has an ID, and every acceptance criterion (AC) becomes at least one automated test or one recorded measurement.

6: 

7: > Numbers marked *initial* (thresholds, weights, targets) are starting values. If you change one after measuring, record the change in the Decisions Log (section 18). Safety thresholds in section 3 are placeholders for you to review against a qualified source and cite in the README; they are not professional advice.

8: 

9: ---

10: 

11: ## 1. Overview

12: 

13: A full-stack web application that combines two things in one place: a **workout logger** with strength analytics (sets, reps, load, estimated one-rep max, personal records, volume, consistency) and a **rule-based diet-plan generator** that builds editable 7-day, multi-cuisine meal plans from a reviewed food and recipe catalogue, with substitutions, a grocery list, and a way to log what you actually ate.

14: 

15: The first release favours **correctness, explainability and testability over opaque AI**. Every number the app shows can be traced to a formula, a catalogue value with a recorded source, or a setting the user chose. The planner is a deterministic scorer with hard safety filters (allergies first), not a promise of an optimal plan, and the app is informational, not medical nutrition advice and not a promise of strength gains.

16: 

17: ### Aim

18: 

19: Build a secure, well-tested full-stack application that lets a gym user record training, see honest strength trends, and generate and adjust meal plans that respect their allergies and preferences, with clear explanations, protective safety rules, and a deployment you can open in a browser on your computer or local network.

20: 

21: ### Inputs

22: 

23: | Input | Details |

24: | --- | --- |

25: | Account and profile | Email, password, display name, timezone, units (kg or lb), optional height, weight and birth date, activity level, goal, and wellbeing settings (section 3) |

26: | Training data | Exercises, routines, sessions and sets (reps, load, optional RPE, rest, warm-up flag) |

27: | Nutrition preferences | Cuisines (several, with a preference level), diet tags, allergies, excluded ingredients, budget, preparation-time limit, target calories and macros |

28: | Meal plan actions | Generate, edit servings, substitute, accept or reject suggestions |

29: | Intake logs | What the user actually ate, by food or recipe and quantity |

30: | Seed catalogue | Reviewed exercises, foods with nutrient values and provenance, and recipes (section 4) |

31: | Configuration | Environment variables: database URL, secrets, allowed origin, registration switch, demo mode |

32: 

33: ### Outputs

34: 

35: | Output | Details |

36: | --- | --- |

37: | Workout history and strength analytics | Per-exercise estimated 1RM, personal records, volume and trends, with every estimate labelled |

38: | Nutrition targets | Editable targets, with the inputs and assumptions that produced any estimate |

39: | Meal plans | 7-day plans with per-meal and per-day nutrient totals, warnings, and an explanation of the filters and scoring used |

40: | Substitution options | Eligible alternatives with nutrient differences |

41: | Grocery list | Aggregated ingredients across chosen days, with units kept consistent |

42: | Dashboard and insights | Consistency, strength trends, planned versus logged nutrition, and explainable observations with their time window, sample size and limitations |

43: | Data export | A complete JSON export of the user's data, and verified account deletion |

44: | Deployed service | The web application, running in containers at `http://localhost:8080` (and over HTTPS on the local network) |

45: 

46: ### Requirements at a glance

47: 

48: - **Functional:** FR-01 to FR-20 (section 12), including the blueprint's FR-01 to FR-15.

49: - **Safety, wellbeing and privacy:** S1 to S10 (section 3).

50: - **Data rules:** DL1 to DL4 (section 4).

51: - **Security:** section 10. **Deployment:** D1 to D8 (section 11).

52: - **Non-functional:** section 15.

53: - **Acceptance criteria:** AC-01 to AC-118 (section 13), mapped to the blueprint's requirements in section 14.

54: 

55: ## 2. Goals, Scope and Non-Goals

56: 

57: **Goals**

58: 1. Accounts with strict per-user data isolation.

59: 2. An exercise catalogue, routines, session and set logging, personal records, estimated 1RM and volume.

60: 3. A reviewed food and recipe catalogue with nutrient values and provenance.

61: 4. Nutrition profile, editable targets, and protective safety rules.

62: 5. A deterministic, explainable, editable 7-day plan generator with allergy-first filtering.

63: 6. Substitutions with recalculated totals, and a unit-aware grocery list.

64: 7. Intake logging, and planned versus actual comparison.

65: 8. A dashboard and descriptive insights that avoid causal claims.

66: 9. Export and deletion of user data.

67: 10. A tested, documented, deployed system.

68: 

69: **Non-goals (v1)**

70: - Medical diagnosis, treatment plans, eating-disorder management or clinical nutrition advice.

71: - Weight-loss or calorie-deficit goals (decision D-11); supported goals are `maintain` and `build_strength`.

72: - Guaranteed optimal plans or guaranteed strength gains.

73: - Wearable integration, barcode scanning, payments, social features, AI chat, and real-time nutrition data from third-party providers.

74: - Email verification, password reset and social login (documented limitations).

75: 

76: **Stretch** (only after every required criterion passes): an integer-programming planner, a nutrition-and-strength association insight (with strong guardrails), rest timers, a custom-food editor, idempotency keys for workout creation, and a public demo deployment.

77: 

78: ## 3. Safety, Wellbeing and Privacy Rules

79: 

80: This app touches food, body data and health-adjacent decisions, so these rules are requirements, not polish.

81: 

82: | ID | Rule |

83: | --- | --- |

84: | **S1 Informational notice** | Every target, plan, log summary and insight screen, and every plan API response, carries a notice that estimates are informational and not medical advice, and that the app is not a substitute for a registered dietitian or doctor. |

85: | **S2 Adults only for nutrition planning** | Nutrition targets, plan generation and estimates require the user to confirm they are 18 or older (`adult_confirmed_at`). If a birth date is given and shows the user is under 18, nutrition planning and estimates are disabled for that account (`nutrition_not_available_for_minors`), with a message recommending guidance from a parent or guardian and a qualified professional. Workout logging and strength analytics stay available. The confirmation is self-declared, which is a documented limitation. |

86: | **S3 Professional-guidance flag** | A profile flag `needs_professional_guidance` (a yes or no only; no condition details are collected) disables estimate-based targets. Targets must then be entered manually, with a banner saying to follow the guidance of the user's professional. |

87: | **S4 Estimated targets are optional and transparent** | Estimates use the Mifflin–St Jeor equation, an activity factor and a goal adjustment (section 5.4), and always display their inputs, formula and assumptions. The user can ignore and edit them. |

88: | **S5 Energy floor** | The app never *suggests* an estimated target below `estimate_floor_kcal` (*initial*: 1,500 kcal); it reports `estimate_below_floor` and asks the user to enter a target manually or seek guidance. A manual target below that value is saved with a warning. Plan generation is **refused** below `plan_minimum_kcal` (*initial*: 1,200 kcal). Review both numbers against a qualified source and cite it in the README. |

89: | **S6 No deficit goals** | There is no weight-loss goal, no deficit calculation and no "calories to lose" language in v1. |

90: | **S7 Wellbeing settings** | The user can (a) **hide calorie numbers** everywhere in the UI (macros such as protein stay visible; the planner still uses calories internally), (b) **pause nutrition** (nutrition features are switched off, training continues, data is kept), and (c) track body weight only by **opting in**: no weight is requested or charted by default, and nothing requires it except the optional estimate, which asks at the moment of use. |

91: | **S8 Neutral language** | Nutrition feedback is descriptive, not judgemental: "within your range" and "below your range", never "failed", "cheated", "bad", "guilt" or streak-loss messaging. A test scans UI strings for a banned word list. |

92: | **S9 Allergy handling** | Allergies and explicit exclusions are hard filters. Catalogue data can be incomplete, so items with unknown or unverified allergen status are excluded when the user has any allergy (setting `exclude_unverified_allergens`, default on), and every plan carries a reminder to check labels. |

93: | **S10 Privacy** | Collect only what is needed. Birth date, height, weight and sex-for-estimate are all optional. Logs never contain passwords, tokens or full email addresses. Users can export and delete everything (FR-15). |

94: 

95: ## 4. Data Rules and Licences

96: 

97: | ID | Rule |

98: | --- | --- |

99: | **DL1 Recorded sources** | Every food has `data_source`, a `source_reference` where possible, a serving basis, a raw or cooked state, and a `verified_at` date. Values that are estimates or imputed are flagged `approximate` and labelled that way in the API and UI. |

100: | **DL2 Licensed data only** | Nutrient data comes from sources whose licence permits this use, recorded in `DATA_LICENCES.md`. Government composition tables such as USDA FoodData Central are commonly public domain, but check each source and each table's licence yourself; if a licence is unclear, do not use the data. |
